question.problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you are given the following data:

$$
f(-4)=2e,\,{f}^{′}(-4)=-e,\,g(-4)=-3e,\,{g}^{′}(-4)=e
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=-4.$
question.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=-4,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=-4} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(-4)g(-4)-f(-4){g}^{′}(-4)}{{g}^{2}(-4)} \\  & =\frac{-e\cdot (-3e)-2e\cdot e}{9{e}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
